title: Campaigns OS QA Verdict Sidecar v0
description: The committed QA verdict sidecar written to .campaign-runtime/qa-verdict.json beside the Build Packet — the artifact campaigns-agent's readback consumes. It is an allowlist PROJECTION of one full verdict (campaigns-os-qa-verdict.v0.schema.json), never a copy: it keeps the same schema_version literal "1.0" (a second version would fork the read end), keeps identity, disposition, per-assertion id/family/page/status/severity/blocked_by, and trimmed exceptions, and empties every URL-bearing field — full verdicts stay gitignored because they carry live storefront URLs, request evidence, and order references. generated_at is stamped at projection/promotion time. Produced only by `qa run` and `qa promote` (never hand-authored), and only from a verdict the projection accepts: a record stamped trusted: false by the QA verdict receiver (an anonymous submission) is refused, so the trust fields can never legitimately appear here. Additions to v0 are expected; consumers must tolerate unknown fields — but the properties this projection deliberately empties or strips are pinned empty/absent below.

schema_version.description: Same literal as the full verdict — the sidecar is the same contract projected, not a second schema lineage.

campaign_slug.description: Carries the Campaign Map ID for schema back-compat, exactly as the source verdict did.

public_route_slug.description: Present only when the source verdict carried a non-null value.

campaign_ref_id.description: Present only when the source verdict carried a non-null value.

generated_at.description: The projection/promotion instant, strict RFC3339 UTC with a Z suffix — the freshness stamp readback staleness checks read. Distinct from completed_at, which stays the source run's own finalization time.

disposition.description: The source verdict's disposition, blocked included: the sidecar records what QA concluded, it is not a pass mark.

base_url.description: URL-bearing — never present in the projection.

entry_urls.description: URL-bearing — always emptied ([]) by the projection.

page_urls.description: URL-bearing — always emptied ([]) by the projection.

tested_urls.description: URL-bearing — always emptied ([]) by the projection.

test_orders.description: Order evidence (URLs, order references, request captures) stays in the full verdict — always emptied ([]) by the projection.

exceptions.description: Re-derived from the PROJECTED assertions, then null-valued keys dropped — so url/expected/actual can never survive into the committed form.

trusted.description: Never present: trust stamps belong to the receiver's stored records, and the projection refuses an untrusted source outright.

blocked_by.description: Tolerated allowlist field for gate-blocked assertions; shape follows the source assertion when present.

expected.description: Stripped by the projection — stays in the full verdict.

actual.description: Stripped by the projection — stays in the full verdict.

evidence.description: Stripped by the projection — stays in the full verdict.

waiver.description: Stripped by the projection — stays in the full verdict.

projectedAssertion.description: The assertion allowlist: id, family, page, status, severity, blocked_by. Everything else — url, expected, actual, evidence, request/response captures — stays in the full verdict.

url.description: URL-bearing — can only derive null from projected assertions, and null keys are dropped.

expected.description: Stripped — stays in the full verdict.

actual.description: Stripped — stays in the full verdict.
